judged_text: retrieved_recently? commits the 60-second throttle key via $redis.setnx before any work is performed and never clears it when perform_retrieve subsequently fails or no-ops, so retries of the failed retrieval are silently suppressed while the job reports success. After one failed fetch the URL is un-retrievable for 60s while the user watches the loading page — sidekiq retries of the raised job and jobs re-enqueued by the page's reload all bail at the throttle and 'succeed' without working; additionally setnx and expire are two separate round-trips, so a worker crash between them leaves 'retrieved:<url>' with no TTL and that embed URL is never retrieved again (permanent loading, zero errors).

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `retrieve` gates work on `retrieved_recently?` (returns true => skips `perform_retrieve`). `retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis throttle key via `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This means the throttle is committed *before* any retrieval work happens; if `perform_retrieve` later fails/raises (e.g., in `fetch_http` / `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), a Sidekiq retry will see the throttle key and skip work, causing the retry to complete successfully without doing the retrieval. Also, because `setnx` and `expire` are separate calls, a crash between them can leave the key without a TTL, permanently suppressing retrieval for that URL.
